Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache
consistent with cervical whiplash injury. The mechanism of the collision is in keeping with the type and degree of force
that would be expected to produce this injury. Over the course of 22 visits, care consisted of physical therapy, manual
therapy, and a home exercise program, and followed a typical recovery pathway with symptoms gradually decreasing
and visit frequency taepring as function improved. Cervical imaging and physical examination findings clearly
corroborate the diagnosis, including reduced range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness. No prior injury or
treatment involving the cervical spine is known to this office. Billing records reflect the services rendered on an
appropriate schedule, with no duplicate or repeated charges for the same service. Paitent is currently improving and
is expected to reach maximum medical improvement with continued home exercise.
